chief_complaint: absence of meaningful speech words, lack of eye contact, and repetitive hand-flapping behaviors in 2-year-old toddler
hpi_details: 24-month-old toddler brought for delay in communication, failure to respond to name, lack of joint attention or pointing, and repetitive lining up of toys scoring high risk on the M-CHAT questionnaire requiring comprehensive developmental multidisciplinary therapy.

Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.

differentials: Global developmental delay from another cause
Language delay alone without autism features
red_flags: Regression of previously acquired skills would be especially concerning

must_ask.objective: Ask about response to name and eye contact
must_ask.say: Does she respond when you call her name, and does she make eye contact with you?

must_ask.objective: Ask about pointing and joint attention
must_ask.say: Does she point to show you things she's interested in?
Have you noticed repetitive movements, like hand-flapping, or lining up toys?
Has her hearing ever been tested, and does she seem to hear normal sounds?
We recommend a comprehensive evaluation with developmental specialists, and early therapy services can make a real difference.

history.answer: We brought our two-year-old daughter in because she is not speaking any words yet and rarely makes eye contact with us.
We first noticed around eighteen months that she was not saying words or looking at us, and her daycare teacher also pointed it out last month.
Her height and weight have always tracked along the fiftieth percentile on her checkups, and she has grown steadily.
She was born full term at thirty-nine weeks weighing 3.2 kilograms without any complications, infections, or newborn intensive care stays.
She eats standard toddler meals and drinks whole milk, but she can be quite picky and gets distressed if foods touch each other.
No, she has never had chronic diarrhea, stomach pain, blood in her stool, frequent infections, or trouble breathing.
She has never had vomiting, seizures, abnormal eye movements, excessive thirst, extreme sensitivity to cold, or constipation.
She rolled over at four months, sat independently at seven months, and walked at twelve months, though she still struggles to use a spoon.
She babbled a little as an infant, but she does not say single words like mama or dada and does not understand simple spoken requests.
She avoids making eye contact when we talk to her, and she rarely turns around or responds when we call her name.
history.topic: Eye contact and response to name

history.answer: She does not point to show us things she wants, and she does not look where we point or copy our gestures.
She flaps her hands when she gets excited or upset, and she repeatedly lines up her toy cars in straight rows for hours.
She passed her newborn hearing screening, has never had an ear infection, and reacts immediately to sounds like crinkling snack wrappers.
No, she has never lost any words or motor skills that she previously knew, she just never developed them.
There is no family history of autism, speech delay, genetic syndromes, or intellectual disability on either side.
She has never taken steroids, stimulants, or any long-term prescription medications.
My husband and I are her primary caregivers, she sleeps well through the night, and we limit television and tablet screens to under an hour daily.
I wondered if she might just have trouble hearing us or fluid stuck in her ears since she doesn't turn when I call her name.
I'm so worried that she won't be able to talk or make friends when she starts preschool next year.
I was hoping to get her hearing tested today and get a referral to a speech therapist who can help her talk.
She has no chronic medical conditions and has never been diagnosed with any illnesses.
She has never had surgery and has never been admitted to a hospital.
She does not take any daily medications, over-the-counter syrups, or herbal remedies, just a standard multivitamin.
She has no known allergies to medications, foods, or environmental triggers.
Neither of us smokes, and she is never exposed to secondhand cigarette smoke.
No, she has never had any contact with alcohol, and no one drinks around her.
She lives in an apartment with both of us, and she attends a small neighborhood daycare three mornings a week.
Both parents are healthy, my height is 165 centimeters and my husband is 178 centimeters, with no chronic conditions in our families.
Her vaccinations are completely up to date according to the national pediatric schedule.
At daycare, her teachers say she plays alone beside other children rather than with them, and she has not been exposed to any infectious illnesses.
